desks.Dividends: Apple, ex Thu Nov 12 at $0.27 per quarter (unchanged, declared with the Nov 2 earnings release; last purchase Wed Nov 11), and Microsoft, ex Thu Nov 19 at $0.98 (up from $0.91, +7.7%, its 24th consecutive annual increase; last purchase Wed Nov 18), are the two capture dates in the next four weeks, and neither carries an information edge. desks.Earnings: Nvidia is the only watchlist name reporting in-window, Tue Nov 17 after close (call 5:00 p.m. ET), with Nasdaq consensus EPS of $2.49; the Nov 20 straddle implies about 9.4-9.8% against a 5.6% average absolute move over the last 12 reports. desks.Futures: Front-month crude fell about 7% on Nov 2 on renewed Qatar-mediated U.S.-Iran contacts, while Gulf exports averaged 17.1 million barrels per day in October, down from 18.9 in September, and Hormuz transits stayed at about half pre-war levels, so the curve prices easing near-term scarcity with tail risk still in place. OPEC+ held December targets unchanged Sun Nov 1. Next catalysts in order: EIA petroleum Wed Nov 4 at 10:30 a.m. ET, EIA gas storage Thu Nov 5, USDA WASDE Tue Nov 10, OPEC+ ministerial Sun Nov 29.
desks.Parity: No published put-call or box parity violation was found for the watchlist. The S&P Dow Jones style-index methodology overhaul, with pro forma files Dec 4 and effective before the open Dec 21, changes growth/value classification, not S&P 500 membership, and matters for style-ETF rebalancing flow around Dec 4-21, not for parity math. A cited estimate puts at least $375 billion in passive funds tied to the affected gauges, attributed and not desk-verified.
desks.Premium: Live 1-day implied volatility prints are SPY 19.6%, QQQ 34.8%, Apple 27.2%, Microsoft 31.1%, Nvidia 41.6% and Tesla 48.2%, against 20-day realized volatility of 11.6%, 22.9%, 14.9%, 20.1%, 31.6% and 36.9% respectively, but the tenor mismatch means no rich-premium verdict is issued. Implied-volatility rank is UNVERIFIED for all six names, and premium into Nvidia's Nov 17 binary is an avoid.
desks.Quant lab: One new candidate was appended to the ledger as row 206, with one WATCH and no TEST and no INTEGRATE movement this run. The WATCH item is Li/Wang on option-implied signals and crash risk (score 48), valued for its regime-conditional reading of the implied-volatility surface: the smirk signal decayed in the current regime while the implied-volatility spread and risk-neutral skewness stayed significant. items.detail: FRED prints dated Nov 2, the latest available, put the effective fed funds rate at 3.88%, the 2-year at 4.59% and the 10-year at 4.91%, a 2s10s spread of +32 basis points, 6 points flatter than the prior session and 9 points flatter over 60 days. SOFR at 3.95% sits 7 basis points over the effective fed funds rate, a normal overnight funding print with no stress signal. Near 5%, the 10-year remains a valuation headwind for long-duration names on discount-rate grounds: a value lens demands a wider margin of safety on long-duration growth exposure, not a sharp repricing of premium assumptions.
items.title: Rates: 10-year at 4.91%, curve sloping up and flattening, funding calm
